insights: Residency is the single biggest lever at almost every top public. The published overall rate badly overstates the odds for out-of-state and international applicants: Georgia Tech ~30% in-state vs ~9% OOS, UNC ~38% vs ~8% (NC law caps OOS enrollment at ~18%), UVA ~23% vs ~9%, UIUC 49.3% vs 29% (OOS) / 30.5% (international), UT Austin reserves ~90% of seats for Texas residents (OOS ~10%), and Berkeley admits CA residents at 14.9% vs 7.3% OOS and 5.5% international.

The 'admission by major' trap is the most important warning for STEM-focused families. Headline rates hide far lower program-level odds: UIUC pure CS ~7% (vs 36.6% overall), UT Austin CS ~8–9% (vs ~22% overall), and Georgia Tech's ~44%-engineering applicant pool. A strong overall profile is not enough — the target major is the real gate.

Test policy now splits the top publics. All three UCs are permanently TEST-FREE / test-blind (SAT/ACT not used at all since Fall 2021), so GPA + essays + activities carry the entire academic signal. Georgia Tech and UT Austin REQUIRE tests (UT reinstated Fall 2025; GT continues, with a University System of Georgia mandate from Fall 2026). Michigan, UVA, UNC, UIUC, and UW-Madison remain test-optional (UW locked through spring 2027).

Selectivity is rising sharply across the board. Georgia Tech hit a record-low 12.7%, UCLA holds near 9% as the most-applied-to U.S. university (~173k applications), UT Austin applications jumped +24% year over year, and UIUC fell from 63% (2020) to 37% (2025). For test-optional schools a strong submitted score still differentiates with no penalty for withholding.
caveats: WebFetch and direct PDF download were blocked in this environment, so exact CDS C9 (SAT/ACT 25/50/75) and C12 (GPA/class-rank) line items were sourced from search summaries and reputable aggregators quoting the official Common Data Sets, not by opening the primary PDFs. The official CDS URLs are cited for each school and should be opened to confirm exact digits before any figure is shown user-facing.
All UC SAT/ACT percentiles are intentionally null because the UC system is test-blind — this is a policy fact, not missing data.

Several middle-50% test ranges are given as p25/p75 with p50 null where a discrete median was not separately sourced. UVA in-state/out-of-state rates vary by cycle and by whether 'international' is bundled with OOS; treat the ~23% in-state / ~9% OOS split as approximate.
